notes: Printed page 218, 'Bilingualism—contd.', Mother-tongue—Hindustani. Column order on this page: Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Konkani, Banajari, Tulu (spellings as in Part I). This scan is faint: the figure 4 frequently prints with its diagonal/crossbar broken so that it resembles 1 (e.g. '14,886' looks like '1·1,886'), and 5/7 and 6/8 are weak. Seven cells were read as damaged glyphs and settled by the printed totals; in every case both the row check (Total of subsidiary languages = sum of languages) and the column check (State excl. C&M = sum of 12 areas) independently require the value recorded: Bangalore District mother-tongue Females 28,906 (6/8 weak; also = Part I); Kolar Gold Fields Total-of-subsidiary upright Females 944 (last digit looks like 1); Kolar District Kannada upright Males 6,024 (last digit looks like 1); Tumkur District Kannada upright Females 11,545 (4 looks like 1); Mysore District Kannada italic Males 14,456 (7/5 weak); Chitaldrug District Total-of-subsidiary upright Females 11,874 (last digit looks like 1); Hassan District Kannada upright Females 5,994 (last digit looks like 1). With these, all row totals, italic totals, State incl. = excl. + C&M and excl. = sum of areas checks pass, and mother-tongue columns agree with Part I. Tumkur District shows Tulu Females 1 upright / 1 italic with no Males; Banajari 2 Males upright (Tumkur) has no italic figure.
